searches.reason: Test whether SASRec uses recent, repeated interests or broad historical associations. Seek practical paired probes using training-prefix holdouts: remove recent events, shuffle order, or replace events with popularity-matched items; measure changes in next-item rank and top-10 stability. Controlled synthetic sequences can verify that each probe detects its intended failure mode without treating sensitivity alone as evidence of quality.

searches.reason: Translate feedback about unsupported compatibility, redundant purchases, and overly broad media matches into evidence-grounded diagnostics. Seek methods using only interaction histories and public titles/descriptions, with lexical retrieval and explicit attributes rather than downloaded pretrained weights. Compare ranking of specific recent-interest matches against broadly related distractors; report unknown specifications separately and avoid inferring ownership satisfaction or incompatibility from missing evidence.
searches.query: recommendation diagnostics intent relevance hard negatives complement substitute compatibility title description evidence abstention user feedback 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Replace raw training margins and average embedding cosine with a trustworthy diagnostic audit. Seek scale-invariant ranking probes, exposure-normalized popularity and history-length slices, bootstrap uncertainty, and controlled parameter interventions that connect failures to embeddings, sequence encoders, or training negatives. Distinguish sampled-candidate performance from full-catalog behavior, and validate diagnostic usefulness against the unchanged macro validation HR@10 within the GPU budget.
